audit.why: 46.94% over 360 games and the chart says Teemo owns levels 3-5 and everything from first item on, with Camille only taking level 1 and level 6. That is an unusually honest chart and it matches the mirror at audits/top/teemo__camille.json, which describes levels 4-5 as Teemo's ownership window and the Hookshot downtime as his lane clock.

Level 6 as Camille's single swing and Teemo's Liandry's/shroom mid-game as the takeover point are both right and both stated on the mirror page. The one number missing was the cooldown arithmetic behind 'his blind cooldown is shorter than your E' — Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank against Hookshot's 16s at rank 1, so he gets two blinds per engage attempt.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet is right that no Teemo ability is ever named — the whole matchup runs on 'his Q blind', 'his E poison' and 'shrooms (R)'. Worse, his kite speed is credited to a passive: 'kites out on passive move speed', 'kites you on full move speed'. Camille's passive is written as 'Adaptive Defense'.
audit.why: Riot's kit is Guerrilla Warfare (P), Blinding Dart (Q), Move Quick (W), Toxic Shot (E), Noxious Trap (R). His move speed is Move Quick, a 14s active — it is a cooldown you can play around, not a permanent stat, which is exactly the kind of thing a player needs to know before deciding whether a step-up gets kited. His passive Guerrilla Warfare is stealth in brush, which is the real reason facechecking for a Hookshot angle is fatal in the side lane — and the text blames only shrooms for that. Toxic Shot is on-hit damage that scales with his attack speed, so armour reads his trades wrong.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named; Move Quick identified as a 14s active rather than a passive; Guerrilla Warfare's brush stealth added to the split-push warning; Toxic Shot named as the on-hit chip; Adaptive Defenses given its real name.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Engage on his blind cooldown' and 'his blind recharges faster than your E' are stated without either number.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is 7s flat and Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s. That is more than two blinds per Hookshot early, which is the whole reason this lane loses — and it turns the vague 'pick the window' into a countable one.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to spikes[2].text and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game section blames shrooms alone for why Camille cannot facecheck to land Hookshot.
audit.why: Guerrilla Warfare makes Teemo invisible while he stands still in brush. Against a champion whose only engage requires walking to terrain, a stealthed Teemo sitting in the exact bush she needs is a separate and larger problem than a trap, and a sweeper answers one of those two, not both.
audit.corrected: Guerrilla Warfare's brush stealth written into late.

edits.before: Your only real swing is Level 6. The honest E-combo line is to bait or wait out his Q blind FIRST, then E-stun in, W-sweetspot for the max-HP slash and heal, and finish with Q — if you dash in on a fresh blind your empowered auto whiffs and you've burned E for nothing. R (Hextech Ultimatum) is the equalizer: cage him and his move-speed kite, blind-and-run, and shrooms all become useless for the duration, so look for the all-in the moment R is up and his blind is down. But his blind recharges faster than your E, so outside of R he can usually answer your re-engage — pick the window, don't force it every wave.
edits.after: Your only real swing is Level 6. The honest line is to bait or wait out Blinding Dart FIRST, then E in, W-sweetspot for the max-HP slash and heal, and finish with the delayed Q — if you dash in on a fresh blind your empowered attack whiffs and you've burned E for nothing. The Hextech Ultimatum is the equalizer: caged, his Move Quick kite, blind-and-run and Noxious Trap are all worthless for the duration, so all-in the moment R is up and the dart is spent. But Blinding Dart is 7s to Hookshot's 16s, so outside of R he simply gets two blinds per engage attempt — pick the window, don't force it every wave.

edits.before: Once items come online Teemo becomes a map problem you can't solve in a straight 1v1. His shrooms carpet every chokepoint and brush around your splitpush, so you can't facecheck to land E; the moment you're revealed, the blind shuts off your autos between dashes and the poison out-chips your sustain while he kites on full move speed. If you didn't convert your Level 6 R windows into a real lead, his split-push and zoning out-value your tempo — sweep his shrooms, respect the blind cooldown, and lean on R-pick teamfights rather than chasing him in the side lane.
edits.after: Once items come online Teemo becomes a map problem you can't solve in a straight 1v1. Noxious Trap carpets every chokepoint, and Guerrilla Warfare stealths him in the very brush you need for a Hookshot wall angle — a sweeper answers the traps, not the champion sitting in them. The moment you're revealed, Blinding Dart shuts off your autos between dashes and Toxic Shot out-chips your sustain while Move Quick carries him clear. If you didn't convert your Level 6 R windows into a real lead, lean on R-pick teamfights rather than chasing him in the side lane.

notes: Two real mechanical corrections beyond the naming: Teemo's kite speed was credited to a passive in three places when it is Move Quick, a 14s active you can play around; and Guerrilla Warfare's brush stealth — the reason a champion who needs to walk to terrain cannot facecheck a side lane — was absent entirely, with shrooms taking all the blame. Reused from the mirror at audits/top/teemo__camille.json: the blind is best spent on the DELAYED second Precision Protocol hit, since that is the one carrying the true damage, and Adaptive Defenses only exists after Camille's own attack lands. Both pages now state the same thing from opposite sides.
